newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine House leader says tax shift likely.
newsitem.headline: Philippine House leader says tax shift likely.

text.p: Philippine House speaker Jose de Venecia said on Tuesday members of the legislative chamber were ready to accept the shift of the excise tax sytem to specific mode, a move which had been approved by the senators.
"We, in the House, are going for a full shift to the specific tax system," de Venecia told reporters after a meeting with President Fidel Ramos.

"We will be able to achieve the maximum revenues for government without hurting the market share of all cigarette and beer companies and without hurting the tobacco planters and without exacerbating consumer prices of these sin products," he added.
Ramos had been pushing for the shift to specific system, whose computation is based on volume, since this would be simpler to enforce and would help plug loopholes allowing large-scale tax evasion.
Earlier, congressmen passed a bill which combined the specific and ad valorem tax system, which is based on the value of the products.

Based on Senate computation, the government stands to gain an additional 7.0 billion pesos in its first three years of implementation if the specific system is adopted, while only 4.06 billion pesos if the House version is passed.
The two houses of Congress are meeting in a bicameral conference committee which is meant to iron out differences in the versions.
